name: Settle up
description: Turn a group's balances into the shortest list of payments that clears them, plus shares/percent splits. Read the money model first, then the split strategies, then the settle-up algorithm, then the UI, then the tests.
commitTitle: feat: settle up and weighted splits

steps.title: The money model
steps.body: Start here. `types.ts` gains a `Transfer` (one payment that moves the group toward square) and widens `SplitKind` to the four strategies. `money.ts` gains `parseAmount`, the single place a typed amount becomes cents. Everything downstream is a function over these shapes.

callouts.body: `Math.trunc` here silently drops a third decimal: `parseAmount('1.005')` becomes 100 cents, not a rejected input. Worth deciding whether that should round or refuse.

steps.title: Splitting by weight
steps.body: `split.ts` adds `exact`, `shares`, and `percent` alongside the existing equal split. `shares` and `percent` divide a total by weight. The contract for the whole file is that a Split's shares sum back to the total it divided.

callouts.body: Each share rounds independently, so the parts can miss the total by a cent (three equal shares of 1000 give 333+333+333 = 999). Compare against how `equalSplit` hands out the remainder just above.

steps.title: Settling up
steps.body: `settle.ts` is the heart of the feature: greedy matching pays the largest debt into the largest credit until everyone is square, in at most n-1 transfers. The invariant to hold in your head is that `totalMoved` must equal `totalOwed`: the money owed does not change just because it took a shorter route.

callouts.body: `owed` is already integer cents (the min of two integer balances), so this round-trip out to major units and back only reintroduces the float error the rest of the codebase is careful to avoid. `const amount = owed` would do.

steps.title: Wiring it into the UI
steps.body: The store gains a `transfers` derived (settleUp over the live balances) and a `settle` action that records a payment as an ordinary expense, so the list recomputes itself. `SettleUpSheet` renders the payments, the balance card grows a Settle up button, and the expense form exposes the new split kinds.

callouts.body: This `{#each}` has no key. The transfer list is fully recomputed on every settle, so an unkeyed each will reuse the wrong DOM rows. Key it by something stable like `from + to`.

steps.title: Tests and release
steps.body: New `settle.test.ts` covers the algorithm (one payment for two people, at most n-1 transfers, every owed cent actually moves). The money and split specs grow cases for `parseAmount` and the weighted strategies. `package.json` adds `date-fns` and `zod`, the changeset describes the release, and the OG image is refreshed.
